title: one route cannot tell apart what needs two observations: a route connected by hand that is silent on UDP is udp_no_reply whatever the cause, and a reset after the ClientHello is tls_sni_or_cert_block_suspected whether the filter is keyed on the name or the address. The automatic connect adds the second observation where another route to the same address gives one (dead address vs UDP stopped: decided); it cannot tell a QUIC-only filter from all UDP dropped

a border that forwards nothing at all, the link itself up, reads as one relay not answering: the automatic connect has no observation outside its routes, and what the host knows of such a network (not validated) is also true of a network that only filters the platform's own check, so total-blackout gets the verdict relay_unreachable and never network_down. Only a host saying kind none gets network_down

a route whose address answers nothing costs a pass two attempt budgets (8 s), not the one (4 s) the automatic connect is meant to stop at: a timed-out connect does not say which phase it died in, the check that settles it runs beside the second attempt, and the stop is looked at between attempts only. Checked two at a time, two silent routes are done in 8.3 s where the stated budget gives 4.5 s
every connect that had the TUN leaves one open file behind for the life of the process: the stop eventfd of gVisor's fd endpoint, which nothing closes when the instance is closed
the Google update channel refuses the standby key in the grouped form `standby promote` prints (appsscript.Build wants the 26 symbols run together; the engine's reader ignores spaces)
